title: Allu Arjun and Lokesh Kanagaraj Are About to Make It Official — and Tollywood Can Barely Breathe
excerpt: AA23 — the long-rumoured collision of Pushpa's swagger and the Leo director's universe — is reportedly heading into a Mumbai trial shoot on June 26. Anirudh on the music, a silver kada glinting in the teaser, and a fanbase that has already decided this is the event of the decade.
body:
It started, as these things now do, with a glint of silver. When the announcement teaser for **AA23** dropped, the internet didn't need a poster or a plot — it needed only a single frame: **Allu Arjun**, the man who turned a beard and a limp into a global movement with *Pushpa*, wearing the iconic silver *kada* that fans instantly recognised as the signature of **Lokesh Kanagaraj**'s cinematic universe. That bracelet did more marketing in one second than most films manage in a year. And now, reportedly, the real thing is about to begin.

According to a report by Aakashavaani, Allu Arjun and Lokesh are in the earliest stages of AA23 — and the team is set to conduct a *trial shoot* in Mumbai on June 26. Not a photoshoot, not a glamour reel. A trial shoot, the kind directors use to lock the look, the lighting, the texture of a film before the cameras roll for real. The film's first official update is expected to land on a grand scale soon after. For a project this anticipated, even a test run becomes a national event.

> Lokesh Kanagaraj's co-writer Rathna Kumar has called AA23 "a proper pan-Indian film" — and given the pedigree, nobody is arguing."**



> Lokesh Kanagaraj's co-writer Rathna Kumar has called AA23 "a proper pan-Indian film" — and given the pedigree, nobody is arguing.


![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)


Let's sit with what this pairing actually means. Allu Arjun is, by most measures, the most magnetic mass hero in the country right now — *Pushpa 2: The Rule* didn't just break records, it rewrote what a Telugu film could do across the Hindi belt and overseas. Lokesh Kanagaraj, meanwhile, has spent the last few years building one of Indian cinema's most obsessively followed shared universes, stitching together *Kaithi*, *Vikram* and *Leo* into a sprawling, blood-soaked saga that fans dissect frame by frame. This is his Telugu debut. Put those two forces in one room and you understand why the hashtag trended before there was anything to actually watch.

The technical roster only sharpens the appetite. **Anirudh Ravichander** — the composer who has become as much a star as the heroes he scores for — is on music, marking his first-ever collaboration with Allu Arjun. The "23 Theme," penned by Heisenberg, has already taken on a life of its own on Instagram Reels, the kind of pre-release earworm that signals a film has captured the cultural moment before a single scene exists. Reports suggest **Pooja Hegde** may play the female lead, reuniting with Arjun after the chemistry they brought to *DJ: Duvvada Jagannadham* and *Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo* — a pairing the audience has been quietly missing.

There's a logistical ballet behind all this, too. AA23 is expected to go on floors only after Arjun wraps **Raaka**, the big-budget **Atlee** spectacle in which the actor reportedly plays four distinct characters across parallel universes, with **Deepika Padukone** confirmed as the female lead and **Rashmika Mandanna** tipped for a key role. That's a CGI-heavy behemoth in its own right. After AA23, he's reportedly lined up to work with *Minnal Murali* director Basil Joseph. In other words: Allu Arjun is booked, blocked, and building an empire one tentpole at a time — a strategy the smartest stars in the industry have all quietly adopted.

For the diaspora, the Lokesh stamp is its own promise. His films travel exceptionally well — slick, propulsive, universal in their action grammar, and reliably given wide overseas theatrical releases across the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf, where the South Indian audience has become a box-office heavyweight. An Allu Arjun film already commands premium NRI showtimes; an Allu Arjun film *directed by Lokesh* will almost certainly open day-one across the diaspora's biggest screens, with streaming to follow on whichever platform wins what will surely be a ferocious rights battle.

Nothing is officially confirmed yet — the makers have stayed characteristically tight-lipped, letting the silver kada and the trial-shoot whispers do the heavy lifting. But that restraint is itself a flex. When you have the biggest mass hero in the country and one of its most worshipped directors, you don't need to shout. You let a single frame, a single theme, a single rumour of a Mumbai shoot send an entire fandom into a frenzy. Watch this space on June 26. If the first look drops the way it's being teased, the rest of 2026's release calendar might just need to make room.
